sentences.text: Welcome back to English for Everyday Life with me and Molly.
Do you love going to the theater?
Maybe you want to watch a play, but you're not sure how to speak English when you're at the theater.
In today's episode, I'll teach you how to speak English at the theater, whether you are buying tickets, asking about a show, or discussing the performance.
This episode is for A1 -level English learners, so I will speak slowly and clearly.
Useful phrases to use before, during, and after the show.
Buying tickets for the theater.
When you go to the theater, the first thing you need to do is buy tickets.
Common phrases.
Hi.
I would like to buy a ticket for the play.
Please.
How much are the tickets?
What time does the play start?
Are there any discounts for students?
Can I buy a ticket online?
Is there a ticket for standing room only?
I'd like to sit in the front row, please.
Example dialogue.
Hi.
I'd like to buy a ticket for Romeo and Juliet, please.
Sure.
Which day would you like to go?
Is there a show on Saturday evening?
Yes.
The show is at 7 p.m.
on Saturday.
I'll take one ticket, please.
Tip.
Many theaters have student discounts or special offers, so always ask if they have any.
If you want to go to a popular show, it's better to buy tickets early because they can sell out quickly.
Asking about the show.
Once you have your ticket, you may have some questions about the play or performance.
Common phrases.
What is the play about?
Who is the director of this play?
Is this show suitable for children?
How long does the show last?
Are there any reviews of this play?
Is there an intermission?
Can I bring food or drinks into the theater?
Example dialogue.
Emily.
Hi.
Can you tell me what Hamlet is about?
Sure.
Hamlet is a tragedy by Shakespeare about a prince who seeks revenge for his father's murder.
That sounds interesting.
How long is the play?
It's about two hours long with a 15 -minute intermission.
Tip.
Before buying your ticket, it's a good idea to ask for the show's description so you know what to expect.
If the show is very popular, there might be a waiting list, so ask about it in advance.

Talking about seats and locations.
When you get to the theater, you may need to ask about seating or where to sit.
Common phrases.
Where is my seat?
Is this seat taken?
Do I need to show my ticket?
Can I sit in the front row?
Is there a better seat available?
Where is the bathroom?
How can I get to my seat?

Yes, that's your seat.
Thank you.
You're welcome.
Enjoy the show.
Tip.
If you have a specific seat number on your ticket, make sure you sit in the correct seat to avoid confusion.
The ushers are there to help you, so don't hesitate to ask them.
During the show.
While the show is happening, there are a few things you might need to say or ask about.
Common phrases.
Could you please be quiet?
I don't understand this part.
This scene is amazing.
What's happening next?
Can I move closer to the stage?
Example dialogue.

I'm trying to hear the actors.
Oh, sorry.
No problem, thank you.
Tip.
Keep your phone off during the performance to avoid disturbing others.
If you need to leave during the show, wait for the intermission.
And if you don't understand something, don't be afraid to ask politely after the show.

Discussing the play after the show.
After the show, you might want to talk about the play with your friends or other people.

I loved the acting.
The scenery was beautiful.
The play was too long for me.
I didn't like the ending.
The music was amazing.
I didn't understand the plot.

When you talk about a play, try to focus on details like the actors, the scenery, and the music.

You might also want to make small talk with people while you wait for the show to start.
Common phrases.
Have you been to this theater before?
How often do you come to the theater?
Do you like live performances or movies more?
What's your favorite play?
What do you think about the theater's design?

Tip.
Small talk is a great way to meet new people and practice conversation skills.
Ask questions, share your thoughts, and enjoy talking with others.
The importance of theater etiquette.
It's important to follow some theater etiquette to ensure everyone has a good experience.
Important etiquette.
Arrive early so you can find your seat before the show starts.
Turn off your phone and keep it silent.
Be quiet during the show.
Don't talk loudly.
Don't take photos or videos during the performance.
Don't leave early, especially if you have tickets for the entire performance.
Respect the actors and other audience members.
Clap at the end of the show if you enjoyed it.
Tip.
If you're unsure about theater etiquette, just follow the audience.
They usually know when to clap or when to be silent.

Final tips for visiting the theater.
Arrive early so you have time to find your seat and get comfortable.
Turn off your phone before the show starts to avoid disturbing others.
Dress nicely as some theaters have a dress code, especially for special events.
Take notes during the play so you can talk about it later.
Relax and enjoy the experience.
Theater is a wonderful way to enjoy art and culture.
